blocks.text: In tree topology, devices are arranged in a hierarchical structure like a tree (as shown in Figure 1.12). It combines features of both bus and star topologies, where multiple star networks are connected to a central backbone. Data flows from the root (main node) to branches and sub-branches. It is easy to expand and manage large networks. However, failure of the backbone can affect the entire network. Tree topology is commonly used in large organizations.

blocks.alt: Tree topology: a vertical Backbone Cable with end caps. Concentrator (hub) S1 joins nodes A, B and C; concentrator S2 joins nodes D, E and F; a third concentrator (hub), fed from S2, joins nodes G, H and I. A server is joined directly to the backbone. Labels: Nodes, S1, S2, Concentrator (Hub), Server, Backbone Cable.
